result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.edge_overlap()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute edge overlap (Jaccard similarity) between this graph and another. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L30204-L30292){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.edge_overlap(other) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge overlap](/assets/graphs/edge-overlap.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two graphs on nodes A to D. G and H share edges A–B and B–D, drawn in accent; A–C is only in G and C–D only in H. The card counts 2 shared edges out of 4 in the union, one unique to each side, for a Jaccard index of 0.5." width="100%"} Edges are compared by node labels. Returns a dictionary with overlap metrics. Each graph is reduced to a set of edges written as `(source_label, target_label)` pairs (a node without a label is represented by its ID as a string). The Jaccard index is the number of edges in both sets divided by the number of edges in either set, so `1.0` means identical edge sets and `0.0` means no edge in common. Because matching is by label rather than by node ID, the two graphs can be built independently, in any node order. This is useful for: - measuring how much a network changed between two conditions or time points - checking how well an inferred network recovers a reference network - comparing networks produced by different construction methods or thresholds A few details to keep in mind. In undirected graphs `A--B` and `B--A` count as the same edge; in directed graphs `A->B` and `B->A` are different edges. Edge weights and attributes are ignored, and parallel edges between the same pair count only once. An unlabelled node is matched on its ID, which may not refer to the same entity in both graphs, so labelled nodes give the most meaningful comparison. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph to compare against. Its edges are matched to this graph's edges by the labels of their endpoints. It should normally have the same directedness as the calling graph: undirected edge pairs are stored in sorted label order, so comparing a directed graph with an undirected one can miss matches. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary with float values under these keys: - `jaccard`: the Jaccard index, from `0.0` to `1.0`. If both graphs have no edges, it is `1.0`. - `overlap`: the number of edges found in both graphs. - `union_size`: the number of distinct edges found in either graph. - `g1_only`: the number of edges found only in the calling graph. - `g2_only`: the number of edges found only in `other=`. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~differential_edges`) : List the edges that differ, rather than counting them. [](`~graph_edit_distance`) : Count node and edge edits needed to turn one graph into the other. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two graphs on the same four nodes share the edges `A--B` and `B--D`, while each has one edge the other lacks. That gives 2 shared edges out of 4 distinct ones, so `jaccard` is `0.5`. Note that `h` adds the shared edge as `B--A`, which still matches `A--B` because the graphs are undirected: ::: {#10f2e06b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "D")]) ) h = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("B", "A"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D")]) ) g.edge_overlap(h) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'jaccard': 0.5, 'union_size': 4.0, 'overlap': 2.0, 'g1_only': 1.0, 'g2_only': 1.0} ``` ::: ::: In directed graphs the direction matters, so an edge and its reverse have no overlap at all: ::: {#e9b9d45d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} d1 = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_node(label="A").add_node(label="B").add_edge("A", "B") d2 = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_node(label="A").add_node(label="B").add_edge("B", "A") d1.edge_overlap(d2)["jaccard"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.0 ``` ::: :::
